Why caching is hard

Cache invalidation is famously one of the two hard problems in computer science, alongside naming things and off-by-one errors. The joke survives because it keeps being true in practice.

The difficulty is not the mechanism. Storing a value under a key and reading it back is trivial. The difficulty is knowing when the stored value stopped being the truth, which is a question about the rest of the system rather than about the cache.

Every caching strategy is therefore a bet about how the underlying data changes. Time-to-live bets that staleness is bounded by a clock. Write-through bets that every writer knows about the cache.
